article_content: After more than a month of waiting, Edward Snowden has finally been permitted to depart from Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport. This comes after he received documentation allowing him a year's asylum in Russia. Snowden, sought by the U.S. for revealing classified intelligence, exited the airport this afternoon following weeks of legal uncertainty. His lawyer, Anatoly Kucherena, stated, 'I have just provided him with documents from the Russian Federal Migration Service permitting him to leave the airport.' Snowden left the airport unnoticed by the numerous reporters present, accompanied by Sarah Harrison from WikiLeaks. WikiLeaks confirmed Snowden's successful acquisition of refugee status and expressed gratitude to those who aided in protecting him. Despite his newfound freedom, Snowden will face stringent restrictions imposed by Russian security agencies. Although he has agreed not to disclose further classified information, concerns remain about potential U.S. data vulnerabilities. The White House has been seeking clarity on Snowden's situation, with Senator Robert Menendez criticizing Russia's decision to grant asylum, stating it damages U.S.-Russia relations. Russian officials, however, insist that the matter is relatively minor and should not affect bilateral ties. Snowden's lawyer mentioned that he has received numerous job offers and attention from Russian women. Snowden also expressed gratitude for the marriage proposals he received, finding them amusing. His lawyer provided him with new clothes and classic Russian literature, including works by Anton Chekhov and Fyodor Dostoyevsky's 'Crime and Punishment.' Russia has dismissed U.S. demands for Snowden's extradition, with officials confirming he will not be sent to any country where his life might be endangered. President Vladimir Putin has stipulated that Snowden must cease leaking U.S. secrets while in Russia.

Jeho právnik Anatoly Kucherena povedal: 'Práve som mu dal dokumenty z Ruskej federálnej migrácijnej služby, ktoré mu umožňujú opustiť letisko.' Snowden opustil letisko nevšimnutý početnými reportérmi, ktorí boli prítomní, sprevádzaný Sarah Harrisonovou z WikiLeaks. WikiLeaks potvrdila, že Snowden úspešne získal štatút utečenca a vyjadrila vďaku tým, ktorí pomohli chrániť ho. Napriek jeho novonadobudnutej slobode bude Snowden čeliť prísnych obmedzení uvalených ruskými bezpečnostnými agentúrami. Aj keď súhlasil, že nebude ďalej zverejňovať utajené informácie, zostávajú obavy o možné ohrozenie amerických dát. Bieli dom sa snaží zistiť situáciu Snowdena, pričom senátor Robert Menendez kritizoval rozhodnutie Ruska udeliť azyl a tvrdí, že to poškodzuje vzťahy USA a Ruska. Ruskí predstavitelia však trvajú na tom, že vec je relatívne nevýznamná a nemala by ovplyvniť dvojstranné vzťahy. Právnik Snowdena spomenul, že dostal množstvo ponúk práce a pozornosti od ruských žien. Snowden tiež vyjadril vďaku za ponuky manželstva, ktoré dostal, a našiel ich zábavné. Jeho právnik mu poskytol nové oblečenie a klasickú ruskú literatúru, vrátane diel Antona Pavloviča Čechova a Fiodora Michajloviča Dostojevského 'Zločin a trest.' Rusko odmietlo požiadavky USA na vydanie Snowdena, pričom úradníci potvrdili, že nebude odoslaný do žiadnej krajiny, kde by mu hrozilo nebezpečenstvo života. Prezident Vladimir Putin stanovil, že Snowden musí prestane uverejňovať americké tajomstvá počas svojho pobytu v Rusku.

article_content: On a Tuesday evening, Texas Governor Rick Perry, known for his public support of Judaism, marked the start of Hanukkah by likening it to the Boston Tea Party, which shared its 241st anniversary that day. While there are similarities, Perry's chosen analogy misses the mark in several ways. Let's delve deeper. The Hanukkah story Perry referenced is straightforward: In the second century B.C., a small group of devout Jews, led by Judah Maccabee, rebelled against the oppressive Seleucid Empire that controlled the Temple in Jerusalem. They surprisingly won, recaptured the Temple, and rededicated it to the God of Israel. Miraculously, the one-day supply of oil for the menorah lasted eight days, leading to the eight-day celebration of Hanukkah. Perry drew a parallel saying, 'The same spirit of freedom that inspired the Maccabees to rise against a foreign empire motivated our Founding Fathers to rebel against the Crown on that fateful night.' However, this analogy has issues. For the Maccabees, the struggle was about religious survival, with the Temple under pagan control. The Boston Tea Party was about excessive taxes, not religious persecution. Moreover, the Boston Tea Party was a symbolic act, while the Maccabees engaged in direct combat. The traditional Hanukkah story is also more complex: the Maccabees fought against assimilationist Jews who had taken control of the Temple with Seleucid support. The miracle of the oil was added much later, in the sixth century A.D. Perry's analogy to the modern tea party movement is more fitting but still flawed. Both groups, originating outside urban centers, uphold traditional values and resist foreign influences. However, the Maccabees' rule eventually became as assimilated as those they overthrew, leading to Roman conquest a century later. Perry's statement that 'Chanukah reminds us of the power of faith to sustain a nation and ensure the security of our ally, Israel' overlooks historical realities. Faith alone does not guarantee national security, as both ancient and modern history show.
translated_content: V utorok večer Rick Perry, guvernér Texasku, známy svojou verejnou podporou judaizmu, oslavil začiatok Chanuky tým, že ho prirovnal k Bostonskému pitnému dni čaju, ktorý v ten deň oslavoval svoje 241. výročie. Hoci existujú podobnosti, Perryho vybrané prirovnanie je v niekoľkých bodoch nesprávne. Ponoríme sa hlbšie. Príbeh o Chanuke, na ktorý sa Perry odvolával, je jednoduchý: V druhom storočí pred Kristom sa malá skupina zbožných Židov vedených Judom Makabejským vzbúrila proti útlaku Seleukovskej ríše, ktorá ovládala Chrám v Jeruzaleme. Prekvapivo zvíťazili, dobyli Chrám späť a znova ho venovali Bohu Izraela. Zázračne jednodenný zásobník oleja pre menóru vydržal osem dní, čo viedlo k osemdňovej oslave Chanuky. Perry vyvodil paralelu: 'Ten istý duch slobody, ktorý inšpiroval Makabejcov, aby povstali proti cudzej ríši, motivoval našich zakladajúcich otcov k vzbure proti Korune v tej osudnej noci.' Toto prirovnanie však má problémy. Pre Makabejcov išlo o náboženské prežitie, keď bol Chrám v rukách pohanov. Bostonský pitný deň čaju bol o prílišnej dani, nie o náboženskom prenasledovaní. Okrem toho bol Bostonský pitný deň čaju symbolickým činom, zatiaľ čo Makabejci sa zapojili do priameho boja. Tradičný príbeh o Chanuke je tiež zložitejší: Makabejci bojovali proti asimilovaným Židom, ktorí prevzali kontrolu nad Chrámom so seleukovskou podporou. Zázrak s olejom bol pridaný oveľa neskôr, v šiestom storočí po Kristovi. Perryho prirovnanie k modernému hnutiu čajovej strany je viac vhodné, ale stále chybné. Obidve skupiny, pochádzajúce z vidieckych oblastí, udržujú tradičné hodnoty a vzdorujú cudzím vplyvom. Avšak vláda Makabejcov sa nakoniec stala takou istou ako tí, ktorých zvrhli, čo viedlo k rímskemu dobytiu o storočie neskôr. Perryho vyhlásenie, že 'Chanuka nás pripomína silu viery na udržanie národa a zabezpečenie bezpečnosti našho spojenca, Izraela', prehliada historické reality. Viera sama osebe nezaručuje národnú bezpečnosť, ako ukazuje staroveká aj moderná história.

PUBLISHED: 11:48 EST, 23 April 2012 | UPDATED: 10:08 EST, 24 April 2012 Banned: Trenton Oldfield, 35, exchanged his wetsuit for more formal attire when he appeared in court. The protester who stopped the Boat Race was yesterday banned from the Olympic torch route and celebrations for the Queen’s Jubilee. Trenton Oldfield, 35, appeared in court for the first time since he swam into the path of the two boats, narrowly missing the oars. The Australian spoke only to confirm his name and address to magistrates. The defendant, who took to Twitter following his arrest to speak out against privilege, showed no emotion as he sat beside his legal team while the charge against him was read out at Feltham Magistrates’ Court in Middlesex. 'You are charged, on April 7 of this year, in the River Thames near Chiswick Eyot, with causing a public nuisance by swimming into the path of the University Boat Race and causing it to stop,' he was told. Michael Schwarz, defending, indicated Oldfield would not enter a plea and his case was committed to crown court. 'The next hearing will be at Isleworth Crown Court,' chairman of the bench Alison Stone told the activist. 'That will be on Wednesday, May 28 at 10 am.' The Australian was released on bail with restrictions preventing him from entering the City of Westminster on May 9 for the state opening of Parliament and forbidding him from going into the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead prior to his next court appearance. During this time, there are a number of events planned in the borough to celebrate the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee. Disruption: Oldfield caused the annual contest on the River Thames to be stopped for around half an hour after he was spotted in the vessels' path as crews battled towards the finish. One condition: The Australian was released on bail with restrictions preventing him from entering the City of Westminster on May 9 for the state opening of Parliament. A further bail condition bans Oldfield from using—or being within 100 meters of—roads which form part of the Olympic torch route until the same date. Struggle: Oldfield—who lives in a run-down block of flats in east London—later defended his anti-elitist stance online, claiming he had always 'fought from within'. The 158th Boat Race on April 7 was labeled 'possibly the most dramatic in history' by organizers after Oldfield created unprecedented disruption. It was the first time in its history that the event was disrupted by a swimmer. This year’s contest also saw an Oxford crew member break an oar before the team’s bowman Alex Woods collapsed after crossing the finishing line. He was later treated in hospital. Oldfield sparked scenes of chaos when he swam towards the boats as they were neck and neck between the two and three-mile marker. Former rower and assistant umpire Sir Matthew Pinsent was said to have alerted fellow adjudicators before the race was stopped and the swimmer, who narrowly avoided the blade of an Oxford oar, was pulled from the river. He was taken away on a police launch and arrested. The race was restarted nearly half an hour later, with Cambridge powering on to victory. Oldfield—who lives in a run-down block of flats in east London—later defended his anti-elitist stance online, claiming he had always 'fought from within'. Dangerous: The 35-year-old swam out to the race before getting caught under the oars of the Oxford team. Drama: The 158th Boat Race on April 7 was labeled 'possibly the most dramatic in history' by organizers after Oldfield created unprecedented disruption. It was not the first time the Boat Race has been temporarily halted. In 2001 the competition was stopped by the umpire just over a minute after the start, following repeated warnings to both crews to move apart and then a clash of blades for which Oxford was blamed. When the race got going, Cambridge rowed to victory. Oldfield, who appeared relaxed during the half-hour hearing, made no comment as he left court.

article_content: Wayne Middleton, a 48-year-old magistrate, is accused of falsely claiming £22,500 in disability benefits while engaging in vigorous physical activities. Despite telling the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) that he couldn't walk without severe pain, Middleton was seen participating in various strenuous tasks during his appearance on Channel 4's Coach Trip in 2011. These activities included downhill grass skiing, abseiling down a 150ft tower, and stilt walking. North Somerset Magistrates Court heard that Middleton, who was diagnosed with Fibromyalgia, began receiving disability living allowance and incapacity benefits in 2003. However, the DWP alleges that Middleton did not inform them about the improvement in his condition and continued to receive benefits from 2005 to 2011. The court was informed that Middleton became so proficient in salsa dancing that he trained as an instructor and conducted at least two 45-minute classes weekly. During his testimony, Middleton asserted that he was still eligible for disability benefits, stating, 'I have to do something with my life, you just can't sit and do nothing. You don't know what it is like to live in pain your whole life, my pain is never going to go away. It doesn't matter what I do, you either do these things or you don't. You have to live with it.' The investigation into Middleton started after an anonymous tip-off. Middleton, who takes 39 tablets daily for his condition, told the court that his doctor advised him to take up salsa dancing. In 2008, he co-founded Salsa Bristol, a dance company, and began teaching others after completing his instructor training. Middleton also volunteered at Bristol Zoo in 2005, helping to feed birds one day a week while receiving benefits. In 2009, he became a magistrate at Bristol Magistrates Court, a role he described as one of his proudest achievements. In 2011, he participated in Channel 4's Coach Trip, where he engaged in demanding activities like abseiling and grass skiing. Middleton denies the charges of dishonestly making false statements to obtain benefits. The trial is ongoing.

Počas svojho svedectva Middleton tvrdil, že stále má nárok na invalidné výhody, a povedal: 'Musím niečo robiť so svojím životom, nemôžete len sedieť a nič nerobiť. Neviete, ako je to žiť v boli celý život, moja bolest nikdy nezmizne. Nezáleží na tom, čo robím, buď tieto veci robíte, alebo neurčite. Musíte s tým žiť.' V roku 2011 sa zúčastnil relácie Channel 4 Coach Trip, kde sa venoval náročným aktivitám ako spúšťaniu sa a trávnatému lyžovaniu. Middleton popiera obvinenia z podvodného udeľovania nepravdivých vyhlásení za účelom získania výhod. Prípad pokračuje.

article_content: In 1993, Romeo Dallaire was optimistic about Rwanda's future. Now a Canadian senator, Dallaire recalls 'shaking hands with the devil' in Rwanda. The Canadian lieutenant general, son of a soldier, was about to undertake his most significant command: leading UN peacekeepers in Rwanda. A year later, he left devastated, witnessing over 800,000 deaths in the Rwandan genocide despite his pleas for reinforcements. Dallaire's mission involved monitoring a peace agreement between Hutus and Tutsis, but it was a façade. Hutu extremists were arming themselves, and Tutsi refugees had formed a rebel army. Dallaire discovered plans for mass slaughter and warned his superiors, but his requests for action were denied. On April 6, 1994, a plane carrying the presidents of Rwanda and Burundi was shot down, triggering the genocide. Dallaire and his troops witnessed horrific violence but had minimal support. International intervention was limited due to recent failures in Somalia. The UN Security Council reduced Dallaire's force by 90%, effectively allowing the genocide to continue. Dallaire refused orders to withdraw, staying to aid humanitarian efforts. The genocide ended after 100 days when Tutsi forces declared victory. article_content: By PA Reporter. Norwich manager Neil Adams will hold talks with left-back Martin Olsson after he appeared to raise his hand to referee Simon Hooper following his dismissal during their 1-0 defeat at Wolves. Olsson was sent off on the hour mark after collecting two yellow cards for challenges on Wolves winger Rajiv van La Parra. Adams, whose side were beaten by a 64th-minute header from Dave Edwards, hopes that Olsson will not face any further action other than a standard one-match ban. Flashpoint: Olsson attempted to stop referee Simon Hooper from producing his red card on the hour mark. Hopeful: Neil Adams said he didn't see the incident but was hopeful that Olsson would avoid a long ban. He said: 'I haven't seen it and hopefully there is nothing in it. But we will have a look at it and see what it is and if there are any consequences from that. I will speak to Martin about that. Of course I will. I didn't see it because as soon as the card comes out you're looking away to what you are going to do. But I will have a look at it.', 'The officials have said nothing to us about any alleged hands on and like I said, I have not seen it for now. We will get the footage going back on the coach. But there has been nothing said or suggested to me as of yet from that. We will need to make inquiries if something has happened.' Despite making the worst possible start to their bid to make an instant return to the Barclays Premier League, Adams refused to be too downcast but admitted that the loss of Olsson was pivotal. In trouble: The Norwich full-back pulls Rajiv van La Parra to the ground to pick up his second yellow. Seeing red: Hooper eventually manages to get his card out and shows it to the Norwich man. He added: 'The second one was a stronger yellow than the first for me. We lost a player at a point where I thought we were controlling the game. We were looking good and pinning Wolves back and when the red card happens we get caught when we are down to 10 men.', 'There were positives to take from the game but you are never happy when you lose.' Edwards, who had missed an excellent chance after just 22 seconds, made no mistake when he rose unmarked to head home Van La Parra's cross. It was a just reward for Wolves who had carried the greater threat all match through Van La Parra, Bakary Sako and Nouha Dicko. Norwich were lightweight in attack, their best chance falling to Lewis Grabban in the 54th minute. Distraught: Olsson trudges off, kicking a water bottle on his way, after being dismissed. Turning point: Adams said he thought the red card marked a change in momentum, allowing Wolves to score. But Grabban was denied a goal on his debut following his £3million move from Bournemouth by a smart save from Carl Ikeme. Wolves manager Kenny Jackett was delighted with his side's performance on their return to the Sky Bet Championship after winning the League One title last season. Jackett said: 'First off it is a good win and a good day for the club. Pressure builds up through pre-season and everyone wants to get to that first day and to get a win on the first day is a big thing. With us coming into a new division that is great. But looking past that there are different types of challenges. You could see the way Norwich defended their goal was very good, and it was an excellent goal that won the game.', 'It was a late run and a very good header into the far corner. There were crucial moments and the sending-off was one. That was pivotal as was Grabban's chance. Then Dave Edwards put that big chance in. They were pivotal moments in the game.'

Olsson bol vylúčený v 60. minúte po tom, čo získal dve žlté karty za fauly na krídľa Wolves Rajiva van La Parru. Adams, ktorého tím prehral gólom Davida Edwardsa v 64. minúte, dúfa, že Olsson nebude čeliť ďalšiemu trestu okrem štandardného jednozápasového dištancu. Budeme sa pýtať, ak sa niečo stane.' Napriek tomu, že začali svoj pokus o okamžitý návrat do Barclays Premier League najhorším možným spôsobom, Adams odmietol byť príliš sklesnutý, ale priznal, že strata Olssona bola kľúčová. Vypadali sme dobre a držali sme Wolves v šachu a keď príde červená karta, chytili sme sa, keď sme boli len desať.', 'Boli pozitíva, ktoré sme si mohli vziať zo zápasu, ale nikdy nie ste šťastní, keď prehráte.' Edwards, ktorý minul výbornú šancu už po 22 sekundách, neurobil chybu, keď vyskočil bez pokrytia a hlavičkou poslal do siete centru Van La Parru. To bolo spravodlivé pre Wolves, ktorí po celý zápas predstavovali väčšie nebezpečenstvo cez Van La Parru, Bakaryho Saka a Nouhu Dicka. Norwich bol v útoku slabý, ich najlepšia šanca pripadla na Lewisa Grabbana v 54. minúte. Zúfalý: Olsson odchádza, kopne fľašu s vodou, po tom, čo bol vylúčený. Zvrat: Adams povedal, že myslel, že červená karta znamenala zmenu v tempe, čo umožnilo Wolves skórovať. Ale Grabbanovi bolo odopreté gólové debut po jeho presune za 3 milióny libier z Bournemouthu dôsledkom chytrého zákroku Carla Ikema. Tréner Wolves Kenny Jackett bol nadšený výkonnosťou svojho tímu pri návrate do Sky Bet Championship po tom, čo vyhrali titul v League One minulú sezónu. Jackett povedal: 'Najprv to je dobré víťazstvo a dobrý deň pre klub. Počas predsezóny sa buduje tlak a každý chce dostat sa k tomu prvnému dňu a vyhrať prvý deň je veľká vec. S naším vstupom do novej divízie je to skvelé. Ale za tým sú rôzne typy výziev. Bolo vidieť, ako Norwich bránil svoj gól veľmi dobre a bol to skvelý gól, ktorý rozhodol zápas.', 'Bolo to neskoro a veľmi dobrá hlavička do ďalekého rohu. Boli kľúčové momenty a vylúčenie bolo jedným z nich. To bolo kľúčové ako aj Grabbanova šanca. Potom Dave Edwards dal tú veľkú šancu. Boli to kľúčové momenty v zápase.'
